english.title: Fail to ensure premises other than slaughterhouse has sufficient number of pens and suitable lairage
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the business operator in respect of premises, other than a slaughterhouse, used for the killing of animals, namely **(..SPECIFY PREMISES..), failed to ensure that

(A)_[a sufficient number of pens was provided at the premises for adequate lairaging of animals with protection from the effects of adverse weather conditions]_
(B)_[the lairage had a floor which minimised the risk of slipping and which did not cause injury to an animal which was in contact with it]_
(C)_[the lairage had adequate ventilation to ensure that temperature, air relative humidity and ammonia levels were kept within limits that were not harmful to an animal, taking into account the extremes of temperature and humidity which may have been expected]_
(D)_[the lairage had, where ventilation was provided other than naturally, a replacement means of maintaining adequate ventilation available for use if the original source of ventilation failed]_
(E)_[the lairage had adequate lighting to enable animals to be thoroughly inspected at any time]_
(F)_[the lairage had, where necessary, suitable equipment for tethering animals]_
(G)_[the lairage had drinking facilities and racks, mangers or other equipment adequate in number and size for the watering and feeding of all animals confined in the lairage, fixed where practicable, and constructed and placed so that they were easily accessible to all the animals, could readily be filled and could not readily be fouled]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 30(1)(d) and 33(1) of, and paragraph 6 of Schedule 2 to, the Welfare of Animals at the Time of Killing (England) Regulations 2015.

other.penalty:
Summary: Fine

Time limit for prosecutions
6 monthsNote
Note that for offences committed since 12 March 2015, section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 removes the limits on certain fines given by the Magistrates' Courts. Offences that were previously punishable by fines of 'prescribed sums' and that were limited to 'not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale' or 'not exceeding the statutory maximum', are now punishable by a fine of any amount.
